Sons of God
sunz uv god
noun phrase (a biblical title)
From the Authorized Version rendering of the Hebrew bene ha-Elohim and the Greek huioi tou Theou; a title used in Scripture of angels, and supremely of believers adopted in Christ.

📖 Biblical Definition

“Sons of God” is a biblical title used in more than one sense, whose crown and fulness is the adoption of believers into the family of God through Jesus Christ. In its highest covenant use it names the redeemed: “As many as received him, to them gave he power to become the sons of God, even to them that believe on his name”; “as many as are led by the Spirit of God, they are the sons of God”; “Behold, what manner of love the Father hath bestowed upon us, that we should be called the sons of God.” This sonship is not by nature but by grace and adoption, for the only-begotten Son is alone the Son by eternal generation; believers are made sons by union with Him, receiving the Spirit of adoption whereby they cry, Abba, Father. The dictionary notes the term's other uses without confusing them: in Job and elsewhere the “sons of God” are the angels, the heavenly host that stand before the LORD; and the disputed “sons of God” of Genesis 6 have been understood variously—most soberly, in the Reformed tradition, as the godly line of Seth intermarrying with the ungodly line of Cain, though some read them as fallen angels or as dynastic rulers. The dictionary does not bind the conscience on Genesis 6 but holds the saving sense as the heart of the title: in Christ, by adoption, sinners become the sons of God, heirs of God and joint-heirs with Christ, awaiting the manifestation of the sons of God when creation itself shall be delivered into the glorious liberty of the children of God.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

A biblical title used of angels (Job 1:6) and supremely of believers adopted in Christ (John 1:12; Romans 8:14); the saving sense—sonship by grace and adoption, not nature—is its crown, with the disputed Genesis 6 usage left unbound.

expand to see more

SONS OF GOD, noun phrase. [Hebrew bene ha-Elohim; Greek huioi tou Theou.] A title used of angels and of adopted believers.

Of believers: to as many as received Him He gave power to become the sons of God (John 1:12).

As many as are led by the Spirit of God, they are the sons of God (Romans 8:14).

This sonship is by grace and adoption, not by nature, through union with the only-begotten Son.

Of angels in Job; the disputed Genesis 6 usage is left unbound, the Sethite reading the soberest.

📖 Key Scripture

Joh 1:12 — "But as many as received him, to them gave he power to become the sons of God, even to them that believe on his name:"

Ro 8:14 — "For as many as are led by the Spirit of God, they are the sons of God."

1 Jo 3:1 — "Behold, what manner of love the Father hath bestowed upon us, that we should be called the sons of God: therefore the world knoweth us not, because it knew him not."

Ga 4:6 — "And because ye are sons, God hath sent forth the Spirit of his Son into your hearts, crying, Abba, Father."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

Liberal theology dissolves the title into a universal “fatherhood of God and brotherhood of man,” making all men sons by nature and denying the sonship that comes only by adoption in Christ.

expand to see more

The great liberal corruption of this title is the doctrine of the universal “fatherhood of God and brotherhood of man,” which holds that all human beings are by nature the children of God, needing no new birth or adoption. The dictionary rejects this on the plain teaching of Scripture. By nature men are children of wrath (Ephesians 2:3); only those who receive Christ are given power to become the sons of God. God is the Father of all as Creator, but the saving sonship—the adoption into His family, the right to cry Abba, Father, the inheritance with Christ—belongs only to those united to the Son by faith.

A second confusion arises from the various uses of the phrase. Because “sons of God” names angels in Job and figures in the contested account of Genesis 6, some build elaborate and speculative doctrines, especially of angelic intermarriage with men. The dictionary counsels sobriety: the Reformed tradition has most often read the Genesis 6 “sons of God” as the godly Sethite line, and the conscience is not bound on the question. What is certain and central is the gospel sense—that sinners become the sons of God by grace, through adoption, in Jesus Christ, awaiting the glorious liberty of the children of God.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

From the Hebrew bene ha-Elohim (sons of God) and the Greek huioi / tekna tou Theou (sons / children of God); the title of adoption rests on union with the only-begotten Son.

expand to see more

Bene ha-Elohim, Hebrew, “sons of God,” used of the angelic host in Job 1:6.

Huioi tou Theou, Greek, “sons of God,” of believers led by the Spirit (Romans 8:14).

Tekna Theou, Greek, “children of God,” the term of John's Gospel and epistle.

Huiothesia, Greek, “adoption as sons,” the grace by which sinners become sons.

“Abba, Father” (Galatians 4:6) is the cry of the Spirit of adoption.

Usage

"The pastor preached that men are sons of God not by nature but by adoption in Christ, against the liberal gospel."

"He counselled sobriety on the “sons of God” of Genesis 6, the Sethite reading being the soundest."

"She marvelled at the manner of love that she, a sinner, should be called a child of God."
